cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.loText: Describe lessons learned from the Equifax case study.
cards.reading: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.statement: Ineffective internal controls at Equifax meant that its monitoring system failed to detect and prevent unauthorized access to sensitive data.
cards.explanation: An expired SSL certificate left Equifax unable to inspect encrypted network traffic, so the intrusion went undetected for about three months. This was a detective-control failure.
cards.originalText: Equifax’s monitoring system failed to detect and prevent unauthorized access to sensitive data.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.loText: Describe lessons learned from the Equifax case study.
cards.reading: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.statement: Equifax employees intentionally disabled security alerts, which allowed hackers to remain undetected.
cards.explanation: No intentional disabling of alerts is reported. The intrusion stayed undetected because an expired SSL certificate was left unrenewed.
cards.originalText: Equifax employees intentionally disabled security alerts, allowing hackers to remain undetected.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.loText: Describe lessons learned from the Equifax case study.
cards.reading: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.statement: Equifax delayed disclosing its 2017 breach, which led to increased regulatory scrutiny and public backlash.
cards.explanation: Equifax announced the breach on September 7, 2017, about six weeks after discovering it, breaching crisis-communication principles and intensifying scrutiny and backlash.
cards.originalText: Equifax delayed disclosing the breach, leading to increased regulatory scrutiny and public backlash.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.loText: Describe lessons learned from the Equifax case study.
cards.reading: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.statement: Equifax immediately informed the public and regulators of its 2017 breach, which minimized reputational damage.
cards.explanation: Disclosure was not immediate: the public announcement came about six weeks after discovery, adding to reputational damage, investigations, fines and lawsuits.
cards.originalText: Equifax immediately informed the public and regulators, minimizing reputational damage.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.loText: Describe lessons learned from the Equifax case study.
cards.reading: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.statement: Equifax could not patch Apache Struts within the expected 48 hours because it lacked a comprehensive inventory of IT assets, so the team could not locate where Apache Struts was used.
cards.explanation: A patch and an alert were available, but without a complete asset inventory the team did not know where the vulnerable software ran.
cards.originalText: A lack of a comprehensive inventory of IT assets, so the team could not locate where Apache Struts was used.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.loText: Describe lessons learned from the Equifax case study.
cards.reading: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.statement: Equifax could not patch Apache Struts because no vendor patch for the vulnerability was available at the time of the alert.
cards.explanation: A patch was released on March 7, 2017, before the alert of March 8, so patch unavailability was not the cause; the lack of an IT asset inventory was.
cards.originalText: The absence of any vendor patch for the vulnerability at the time of the alert.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.loText: Describe lessons learned from the Equifax case study.
cards.reading: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.statement: A lack of sufficient internal phishing exercises was identified as a key weakness in Equifax's information security management.
cards.explanation: The five key weaknesses were an insufficient IT asset inventory, unenforced patch management, inconsistent internal communication, an expired SSL certificate and poor external communication. The attack was a technical exploit, not phishing.
cards.originalText: Lack of sufficient internal phishing exercises.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.loText: Describe lessons learned from the Equifax case study.
cards.reading: ORR-9: Cyberthreats and Information Security Risks
cards.statement: Using an expired digital certificate was identified as a key weakness in Equifax's information security management.
cards.explanation: The expired SSL certificate left Equifax unable to inspect encrypted traffic, so the intruders went undetected for months.
cards.originalText: Using an expired digital certificate.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Under the Basel Committee's AML/CFT guidance, the first line of defense should put AML/CFT policies and procedures in writing, communicate them to all personnel, and provide ongoing training tailored to each role.
cards.explanation: A culture of compliance is built through clear written policies, communication to all staff, high ethical standards and ongoing role-tailored training, including for new hires and refreshers.
cards.originalText: Put AML/CFT policies and procedures in writing, communicate them to all personnel, and provide ongoing training tailored to each role.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: The head of the business line should manage the independent testing of the AML/CFT programme.
cards.explanation: Independent testing belongs to internal audit, the third line of defense. Business-line involvement would undermine its independence.
cards.originalText: Have the head of the business line manage the independent testing of the AML/CFT programme.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: AML/CFT training should be provided once, at hiring, and only to front-office staff.
cards.explanation: Basel calls for ongoing, role-tailored training and refreshers for staff across functions, not one-off training of front-office staff only.
cards.originalText: Provide AML/CFT training once, at hiring, and only to front‑office staff.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Under the Basel Committee's recommendations, a bank should appoint a qualified chief AML/CFT officer with sufficient stature and authority and a direct reporting line to senior management or the board, and with no business-line or internal audit responsibilities.
cards.explanation: Independence, authority and direct access to the board are the core governance requirements; the officer should not have business-line, data protection or internal audit duties, to avoid conflicts of interest.
cards.originalText: Appoint a qualified chief AML/CFT officer with sufficient stature and authority, a direct reporting line to senior management or the board, and no business‑line or internal audit responsibilities.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank's chief AML/CFT officer can also head internal audit in order to economize on resources.
cards.explanation: Combining the roles is a conflict of interest. The chief AML/CFT officer is the second line of defense and should not be responsible for internal audit, the third line.
cards.originalText: Appoint a chief AML/CFT officer who also heads internal audit, to economize on resources.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank's chief AML/CFT officer should report through the head of the largest business line.
cards.explanation: Reporting through a business line subordinates compliance to business interests. The officer should have a direct reporting line to senior management or the board.
cards.originalText: Have the chief AML/CFT officer report through the head of the largest business line.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Incoming payments from unrelated third-party accounts that are inconsistent with an account's stated purpose are a key money laundering red flag that monitoring should capture.
cards.explanation: Basel monitoring systems should detect inconsistencies with a customer's expected transactional profile. Receipts from unrelated third parties do not fit the stated purpose and may obscure the source of funds.
cards.originalText: Incoming payments come from unrelated third‑party accounts, inconsistent with the stated purpose of the account.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Under the Basel Committee's AML/CFT framework, the main role of supervisors is to evaluate whether a bank has an appropriate and reasonable risk assessment and an AML/CFT programme that reflects its inherent risks.
cards.explanation: Supervisors take a risk-based approach and independently evaluate the adequacy of the bank's risk assessment and the effectiveness of its controls; they review and challenge rather than design or run the bank's systems.
cards.originalText: Evaluating whether the bank has an appropriate and reasonable risk assessment and an AML/CFT programme that reflects its inherent risks.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Under the Basel Committee's AML/CFT framework, the main role of supervisors is the approval and oversight of a bank's AML/CFT risk management policies and procedures.
cards.explanation: Approval and oversight of AML/CFT policies and procedures is the responsibility of the bank's board and senior management. Supervisors evaluate the bank's risk assessment and controls.
cards.originalText: Approval and oversight of AML/CFT risk management policies and procedures.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: In the second line of defense, the chief AML/CFT officer is responsible for ongoing monitoring of the bank's fulfilment of its AML/CFT duties.
cards.explanation: Second-line oversight includes sample testing of compliance and review of exception reports, with alerts to senior management or the board where needed.
cards.originalText: Ongoing monitoring of the bank’s fulfilment of its AML/CFT duties.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: The chief AML/CFT officer in the second line of defense is responsible for conducting customer due diligence checks.
cards.explanation: Customer due diligence is carried out by the business units, the first line of defense. The chief AML/CFT officer monitors and oversees.
cards.originalText: Conducting customer due diligence checks.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: In a bank's AML/CFT framework, internal audit is responsible for independently evaluating the effectiveness of risk management and controls.
cards.explanation: Internal audit is the third line of defense; it evaluates rather than operates the controls, and reports to the audit committee or board.
cards.originalText: Independently evaluating the effectiveness of risk management and controls.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Internal audit is responsible for developing a bank's AML/CFT policies and procedures.
cards.explanation: Policy development is a management responsibility, with approval and oversight by the board. An audit function that wrote the policies would impair its independence when auditing them.
cards.originalText: Developing AML/CFT policies and procedures.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: The supervisor is one of the three lines of defense for AML/CFT in a bank.
cards.explanation: The three lines of defense are internal to the bank: business units, the chief AML/CFT officer and compliance, and internal audit. The supervisor provides external oversight.
cards.originalText: The supervisor
cards.correction: Internal audit is one of the three lines of defense for AML/CFT in a bank.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Customer-facing activities form the first line of defense for AML/CFT in a bank.
cards.explanation: Business units and customer-facing activities are the first line; the second line is the chief AML/CFT officer and compliance; the third is internal audit.
cards.originalText: Customer‑facing activities

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: To apply a risk-based approach, a bank must understand its inherent ML/FT risks in its customer base, products and services, delivery channels, and the jurisdictions in which it and its customers operate.
cards.explanation: Basel requires understanding of ML/FT risk across customers, products and services, delivery channels (including products in development) and jurisdictions, with controls and monitoring commensurate with those risks.
cards.originalText: Its customer base, products and services, delivery channels, and the jurisdictions in which it and its customers operate.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank can understand its inherent ML/FT risks using only the transaction data generated by its own systems.
cards.explanation: Basel expects internal data (operational and transaction data) to be combined with external sources such as national risk assessments and country reports from international organizations.
cards.originalText: Only the transaction data generated by its own systems.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Audits of a bank's AML/CFT framework should be performed independently by internal audit rather than by the chief AML/CFT officer.
cards.explanation: The chief AML/CFT officer is the second line of defense and should not be responsible for internal audit. Self-review lacks independence, so the third-line internal audit must test the programme.
cards.originalText: The audit should be performed independently (internal audit), not by the chief AML/CFT officer.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank should integrate international risk assessments and country reports to augment its internal monitoring when managing ML/FT risks.
cards.explanation: Understanding inherent ML/FT risk rests on both internal data and external sources such as national risk assessments and country reports from international organizations.
cards.originalText: Integrate international risk assessments and country reports to augment the bank’s internal monitoring.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank should prioritize customer due diligence rules as the sole tool for ML/FT risk identification.
cards.explanation: CDD is one control among several; risk identification looks at customers, products and services, delivery channels and jurisdictions using internal and external information.
cards.originalText: Prioritize CDD rules as the sole tool for risk identification.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank should delegate responsibility for day-to-day ML/FT risk management to its board of directors.
cards.explanation: The board approves and oversees AML/CFT policies; senior management and the chief AML/CFT officer manage the risks.
cards.originalText: Delegate responsibility for ML/FT risk management to the board of directors.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank's chief AML/CFT officer should have a direct reporting line to senior management or the board, and the relationship between the chief officer and other officers should be clearly defined.
cards.explanation: A direct reporting line gives the officer independence and stature and ensures ML/FT issues reach the board; where duties are separate from the CRO or chief compliance officer, their roles must be clearly defined.
cards.originalText: Ensure that the Chief AML/CFT officer has a direct reporting line to senior management or the board, clarifying the relationship between the chief officer and other officers.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: AML/CFT training content should be standardized so that it is identical for all departments of a bank.
cards.explanation: Training should be tailored to staff function, job responsibility and risk exposure rather than being identical for everyone.
cards.originalText: Standardize the AML/CFT training content for all departments to maintain uniformity in knowledge dissemination across the bank.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank's chief AML/CFT officer should be the sole authority to modify the bank's AML/CFT policies without consulting the board or senior management.
cards.explanation: AML/CFT policies are approved and overseen by the board and senior management; unilateral authority would remove governance checks.
cards.originalText: Allocate the Chief AML/CFT officer as the sole authority to modify and adjust bank AML/CFT policies without consulting the board or senior management.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Effective AML/CFT risk management requires robust communication between the three lines of defense, with the first line (business units) proactively identifying, assessing and controlling AML/CFT risks.
cards.explanation: Business units own the day-to-day identification, assessment and control of ML/FT risk, supported by coordination with the chief AML/CFT officer (second line) and internal audit (third line).
cards.originalText: Facilitate robust communication channels between the three lines of defense, ensuring that the first line ‑ business units, are proactive in identifying, assessing, and controlling AML/CFT risks.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Internal audit should be the primary decision-maker for amending a bank's AML/CFT policies.
cards.explanation: Internal audit is the independent third line that evaluates controls; making policy decisions would compromise its independence.
cards.originalText: Assign the internal audit function as the primary decision‑maker for amending AML/CFT policies, thereby ensuring an unbiased review and implementation process.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank's compliance function can rely on advanced technology tools for AML/CFT monitoring while relegating human intervention to the background.
cards.explanation: Technology supports monitoring, but staff judgment, training and suspicious-transaction reporting remain essential.
cards.originalText: Empower the compliance function with advanced technology tools, relegating human intervention to the background, for efficient and error‑free monitoring.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Internal audit should conduct periodic, risk-based audits of AML/CFT policies, staff implementation, compliance oversight and training, including bank-wide audits and an evaluation of the IT monitoring system, and should proactively follow up its findings.
cards.explanation: Internal audit provides independent, periodic, risk-based assurance over the whole AML/CFT framework, with frequency set by risk, and follows up on its findings.
cards.originalText: Conduct periodic, risk‑based audits of AML/CFT policies, staff implementation, compliance oversight and training, including bank‑wide audits and an evaluation of the IT monitoring system, and proactively follow up findings.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Internal audit should take over responsibility for amending AML/CFT policies so that policy formulation is independent.
cards.explanation: Policy is approved and overseen by the board and senior management. Owning policy would compromise internal audit's independence.
cards.originalText: Take over responsibility for amending AML/CFT policies so that policy formulation is independent.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Internal audit work on AML/CFT should be limited to post-incident reviews so that it does not overlap with the work of the second line.
cards.explanation: Internal audit performs periodic, risk-based evaluations of controls, not only post-incident reviews.
cards.originalText: Limit audit work to post‑incident reviews so that it does not overlap with the work of the second line.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Absolute customer confidentiality that prevents a bank from monitoring customer activity and proactively reporting suspicious activity is inappropriate.
cards.explanation: Basel requires ongoing monitoring of business relationships and procedures to detect and report suspicious transactions; customer confidentiality cannot override this.
cards.originalText: Absolute confidentiality is incorrect because the bank must monitor (and document) activity and should report suspicious activity

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: The three lines of defense do not apply to ML/FT risks because only two of them can effectively play a role.
cards.explanation: The three lines (business units, the chief AML/CFT officer, and internal audit) apply fully to ML/FT risk, and the chief officer may also be the CRO.
cards.originalText: The three lines of defense do not apply to ML/FT risks because only two can effectively play a role

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank cannot build profiles of customers' normal activity because of discrimination laws.
cards.explanation: Building a profile of normal activity for each customer or business relationship is recommended so that abnormal activity can be identified.
cards.originalText: The bank cannot generate profiles of customers due to discrimination laws

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: In the three lines of defense model for AML/CFT, internal audit is the independent third line and reports directly to the board's audit committee.
cards.explanation: Internal audit independently evaluates risk management and controls and reports to the audit committee or board.
cards.originalText: The internal audit division performs quarterly AML/CFT reviews and reports directly to the board’s audit committee.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Internal and external auditors should evaluate a bank's risk controls to ensure that they are effective in managing ML/FT risk and compliant with regulations.
cards.explanation: Internal audit is the third line of defense, and external auditors can also evaluate AML/CFT policies and controls for effectiveness and compliance.
cards.originalText: Internal and external auditors should evaluate the bank’s risk controls to ensure that they are effective in managing ML/FT risk as well as compliant with regulations.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: The CRO should serve as the primary point of contact with regulatory supervisors and financial intelligence units on ML/FT risk issues.
cards.explanation: The chief AML/CFT officer is the contact point for supervisors and financial intelligence units; the CRO would only be so if also acting as chief AML/CFT officer.
cards.originalText: The CRO should serve as the primary point of contact with regulatory supervisors and financial intelligence units on any issues related to ML/FT risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Monitoring ML/FT risk by reviewing only transactions above a set threshold value is consistent with best practice.
cards.explanation: A value threshold leaves sub-threshold transactions unmonitored and invites structuring. Monitoring should be risk-based and cover all accounts and transactions.
cards.originalText: Establish a threshold transaction value and review all transactions above this threshold for evidence of ML/FT.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Politically exposed persons (PEPs) can be excluded from ML/FT screening because their ML/FT risk is much lower.
cards.explanation: PEPs are higher-risk customers, and foreign PEPs in particular require enhanced due diligence.
cards.originalText: Exclude politically exposed persons (PEPs) from screening for ML/FT risk due to their much lower ML/FT risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Compliance and legal functions have the primary responsibility for managing a bank's ML/FT risk.
cards.explanation: The first line of defense, the business units, holds primary responsibility for the ML/FT risk of their activities. Compliance is part of the second line, with the chief AML/CFT officer overseeing.
cards.originalText: Give the compliance and legal functions the primary responsibility for managing ML/FT risk.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Regulatory authorities are one of the three lines of defense a bank uses to mitigate ML/FT risks.
cards.explanation: The three lines of defense are internal to the bank: business units, the chief AML/CFT officer and compliance, and internal audit. Regulatory authorities supervise from outside.
cards.originalText: Regulatory authorities.
cards.correction: Internal audit is one of the three lines of defense a bank uses to mitigate ML/FT risks.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: The chief ML/FT officer sits in the second line of defense in managing a bank's ML/FT risks.
cards.explanation: The second line consists of the chief AML/CFT officer and the compliance function; the first line is the business units and the third is internal audit.
cards.originalText: The chief ML/FT officer.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: The chief ML/FT officer should perform customer due diligence at account opening for all high-risk customers.
cards.explanation: Onboarding CDD is a first-line task performed by the business units. The chief officer is second line and oversees and advises.
cards.originalText: The chief ML/FT officer should perform customer due diligence at account opening for all high‑risk customers.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Business units should file suspicious activity reports directly with the financial intelligence unit without escalating to the compliance function.
cards.explanation: Reporting suspicious transactions to the financial intelligence unit is the chief AML/CFT officer's responsibility; business units detect and escalate.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank's board of directors should review individual customer files to confirm that due diligence has been performed correctly.
cards.explanation: The board approves and oversees strategy and policy; reviewing individual customer files is an operational task.
cards.originalText: The board of directors should review individual customer files to confirm that due diligence has been performed correctly.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Country reports from international organizations are an example of external data that a chief AML/CFT officer should analyze to manage and mitigate ML/FT risks.
cards.explanation: Risk understanding rests on internal data (operational and transaction data) and external sources such as national risk assessments and country reports from international organizations.
cards.originalText: Country reports.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Transaction data is an example of external data that a chief AML/CFT officer should analyze to manage and mitigate ML/FT risks.
cards.explanation: Transaction data is collected by the bank itself, so it is internal data. External sources include national risk assessments and country reports from international organizations.
cards.originalText: Transaction data.
cards.correction: Transaction data is an example of internal data that a chief AML/CFT officer should analyze to manage and mitigate ML/FT risks.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Bank tellers and branch managers are examples of the first line of defense in managing and mitigating ML/FT risks.
cards.explanation: Customer-facing business units are the first line and own the ML/FT risks of their activities, using written policies to identify, assess and control them.
cards.originalText: the first line of defense.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: ML/FT risk is the sole responsibility of the chief AML/CFT officer, so front-line staff such as tellers and branch managers fall outside the lines of defense.
cards.explanation: ML/FT risk is not left to one officer. Customer-facing staff are the first line of defense and must follow policies and detect and report suspicious activity.
cards.originalText: staff outside the lines of defense, because ML/FT risk is the sole responsibility of the chief AML/CFT officer.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: The Basel Committee is committed to sound AML/CFT policies in banks in order to strengthen the safety and soundness of banks and preserve the integrity of the international financial system.
cards.explanation: The Committee writes from a prudential mandate. Banks without sound ML/FT risk management face reputational, operational, compliance and concentration risks, which threaten their safety and soundness.
cards.originalText: To strengthen the safety and soundness of banks and preserve the integrity of the international financial system

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain best practices recommended by the Basel committee for the assessment, management, mitigation, and monitoring of money laundering and financing of terrorism (ML/FT) risks.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: The Basel Committee's AML/CFT work aims to enforce the Financial Action Task Force recommendations as binding law on banks.
cards.explanation: The Committee builds on FATF standards but does not enforce them or make them binding; it issues supervisory guidance.
cards.originalText: To enforce the Financial Action Task Force recommendations as binding law on banks

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: If a bank cannot complete customer identity verification after processing a first transaction, it should consider filing a suspicious transaction report (STR) without informing the customer, directly or indirectly, that it has been or will be filed.
cards.explanation: Failure to complete CDD triggers consideration of an STR, and tipping off the customer is prohibited.
cards.originalText: Consider filing an STR, without informing the customer, directly or indirectly, that it has been or will be filed

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank that is filing a suspicious transaction report (STR) should notify the customer so that the customer can supply further documents.
cards.explanation: Informing the customer, directly or indirectly, that an STR has been or will be filed is tipping off, which is prohibited.
cards.originalText: Notify the customer that a suspicious transaction report (STR) is being filed so the customer can supply documents

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank's customer acceptance policy should apply differentiated due diligence measures based on factors such as the customer's geographical location, the type of product desired and the customer's risk level, balancing risk management with non-discrimination.
cards.explanation: A risk-based customer acceptance policy manages ML/FT risk without excluding financially or socially disadvantaged people; basic due diligence applies to all customers and rises with risk.
cards.originalText: Develop a CAP that incorporates differentiated due diligence measures, considering factors such as the customer’s geographical location, type of product desired, and the level of risk associated with their profile, to balance risk management with non‑discrimination.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A customer acceptance policy should mandate enhanced due diligence for all new customers, irrespective of their risk profile.
cards.explanation: Enhanced due diligence for everyone ignores the risk-based approach and is excessively restrictive. Due diligence should be commensurate with risk.
cards.originalText: Enforce a stringent CAP that mandates enhanced due diligence for all new customers, irrespective of their risk profile, to maintain a consistent level of scrutiny across all customer interactions.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A customer acceptance policy should restrict the opening of accounts to customers who can provide a comprehensive financial profile.
cards.explanation: Such a restriction would exclude low-balance or disadvantaged customers, contradicting financial inclusion. The policy must not be so restrictive that it denies access to the disadvantaged.
cards.originalText: Implement a universal policy that restricts the opening of accounts to only those customers who can provide a comprehensive financial profile, thereby minimizing the risk of money laundering and terrorist financing.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: As a general rule, a customer's identity should be established and verified before the bank opens the account or carries out any transactions.
cards.explanation: Basel says a bank should generally not establish a relationship or carry out transactions until the customer's identity is satisfactorily established and verified.
cards.originalText: As a general rule, Jack’s identity should be established and verified before the bank opens the account or carries out any transactions

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Because a customer is high-risk, a bank is required to avoid taking that customer on.
cards.explanation: A bank may accept high-risk customers, applying enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval; high risk does not mean prohibited.
cards.originalText: Because Jack is a high‑risk customer, the bank is required to avoid him like any high‑risk customer

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A customer who already has an account at a reputable bank can be classified as low-risk and well-identified.
cards.explanation: A prior account elsewhere does not establish low risk or verified identity; the other bank may even have refused or ejected the customer over ML/FT concerns.
cards.originalText: Because Jack already has an account at a reputable bank, he can be classified as low‑risk and well‑identified

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A politically exposed person (PEP) can be classified as low-risk on the assumption that the media already vets them.
cards.explanation: PEPs, especially foreign PEPs, are higher risk and need enhanced due diligence; media scrutiny does not lower the risk.
cards.originalText: If Jack is a politically exposed person (PEP), he can be classified as low‑risk on the assumption that the media already vets him and he cannot evade scrutiny

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Foreign politically exposed persons, including through trusts funded from large and varied overseas sources, call for enhanced due diligence.
cards.explanation: EDD is triggered by risk features such as foreign PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, complex structures and unknown beneficial owners, and large varied foreign funding adds to the risk.
cards.originalText: A trust for a foreign politically exposed person (PEP), funded from large and varied overseas sources

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Enhanced customer due diligence is appropriate for accounts with large balances and regular cross-border wire transfers.
cards.explanation: Basel notes that EDD may be essential for an individual planning a large account balance with regular cross-border wires; EDD is risk-based and targeted at higher-risk features.
cards.originalText: accounts with large balances and regular cross‑border wire transfers.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Describe recommended practices for the acceptance, verification, and identification of customers at a bank.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Enhanced customer due diligence is required for all accounts from customers initiated in countries outside the bank's home country.
cards.explanation: Country of origin is one input to the customer risk profile, not an automatic trigger for enhanced due diligence.
cards.originalText: all accounts from customers initiated in countries outside the United States.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain practices for managing ML/FT risks in a group-wide and cross-border context.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank may rely on customer due diligence performed by an introducer in the same financial group that is subject to the same standards as the bank, with those standards supervised at group level, while the bank still obtains the customer information.
cards.explanation: Reliance on an introducer requires standards at least as strict as the bank's, and ultimate responsibility for CDD remains with the bank.
cards.originalText: Rely on an introducer in the same financial group that is subject to the same standards as the bank, with application of those standards supervised at group level, while the bank still obtains the customer information

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain practices for managing ML/FT risks in a group-wide and cross-border context.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank may rely on an introducer subject to less strict AML/CFT standards than its own, provided the introducer has a strong written AML policy.
cards.explanation: Basel says a bank should not rely on introducers subject to less strict standards; a policy on paper does not cure the gap.
cards.originalText: Rely on an introducer subject to less strict AML/CFT standards than the bank’s own, provided the introducer has a strong written AML policy

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain practices for managing ML/FT risks in a group-wide and cross-border context.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank's responsibility for customer due diligence ends once an introducer in any jurisdiction confirms that identification was completed.
cards.explanation: Ultimate responsibility for CDD remains with the bank; relying on an introducer does not discharge it.
cards.originalText: Rely on an introducer in any jurisdiction, because the bank’s responsibility for CDD ends once the introducer confirms identification was completed

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain practices for managing ML/FT risks in a group-wide and cross-border context.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A bank group's customer due diligence process can be applied uniformly worldwide, with no country-specific adaptations, and still align with Basel Committee best practices.
cards.explanation: Group-wide consistency does not mean identical procedures everywhere. Where a host jurisdiction's requirements are stricter than group policy, the branch or subsidiary must adopt the host requirements.
cards.originalText: The ”QuickVerify” system streamlines customer due diligence with a uniform global approach, eliminating duplication by foregoing country‑specific adaptations.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain practices for managing ML/FT risks in a group-wide and cross-border context.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Monitoring that flags atypical transactions in high-risk accounts for further review reflects the risk-based approach that the Basel Committee recommends.
cards.explanation: Basel monitoring systems should detect unusual or inconsistent activity, with intensity commensurate with risk.
cards.originalText: ”Borderless Monitor” flags atypical transactions in high‑risk accounts for further review.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain practices for managing ML/FT risks in a group-wide and cross-border context.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: Wire transfers should carry detailed sender (originator) and recipient (beneficiary) information.
cards.explanation: Wire transfers should carry full originator and beneficiary information, and these should be subject to monitoring.
cards.originalText: All wire transfers include detailed sender and recipient information, reviewed manually and automatically.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain practices for managing ML/FT risks in a group-wide and cross-border context.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: When a host country's customer due diligence requirements are stricter than the group's AML/CFT policy, the group policy should still be applied at the subsidiary to keep procedures uniform.
cards.explanation: Group-wide consistency does not override stricter host requirements; the subsidiary must adopt the host-country requirements.
cards.originalText: Apply the group policy at the subsidiary to keep procedures uniform, since group‑wide consistency takes precedence over local rules.
cards.correction: When a host country's customer due diligence requirements are stricter than the group's AML/CFT policy, the subsidiary should adopt the host requirements.

changes.from: the group policy should still be applied at the subsidiary to keep procedures uniform
changes.to: the subsidiary should adopt the host requirements

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.loText: Explain practices for managing ML/FT risks in a group-wide and cross-border context.
cards.reading: ORR-10: Sound Management of Risks related to Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism
cards.statement: A subsidiary should adopt a host country's customer due diligence requirements where they are stricter than the group's AML/CFT policy.
cards.explanation: Group policies must be applied consistently but remain consistent with local rules; stricter host requirements are adopted locally, while the group chief AML/CFT officer coordinates legally protected information sharing and informs home supervisors if FATF standards cannot be implemented.
cards.originalText: Allow the subsidiary to adopt Country F’s stricter requirements, and have the group chief AML/CFT officer coordinate information sharing with the head office within legal protections, informing home supervisors if FATF standards cannot be properly implemented.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Under the EU Directive, money laundering includes knowingly converting or transferring property derived from criminal activity in order to disguise its illicit origin.
cards.explanation: The EU Directive of 20 May 2015 treats conversion or transfer of property known to derive from criminal activity, to conceal or disguise its illicit origin, as money laundering.
cards.originalText: Knowingly converting or transferring property derived from criminal activity in order to disguise the illicit origin of the property.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: The provision or collection of funds to be used, partly or in full, to facilitate any offense considered a terrorist act constitutes money laundering.
cards.explanation: Providing or collecting funds to facilitate terrorist acts is terrorist financing, a separate offence from money laundering.
cards.originalText: The provision or collection of funds to be used, partly or in full, to facilitate any offense considered by the authorities as a terrorism act.
cards.correction: The provision or collection of funds to be used, partly or in full, to facilitate any offense considered a terrorist act constitutes terrorist financing.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Any intentional violation of the law or of internal policies perpetrated by a firm's employees constitutes money laundering.
cards.explanation: That describes unauthorized activities, a subcategory of internal fraud, not money laundering.
cards.originalText: Any intentional violation of the law or of internal policies perpetrated by the firm’s employees.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Financial crime is any criminal conduct relating to money or to financial services or markets.
cards.explanation: The UK FCA defines financial crime broadly as criminal conduct relating to money, financial services or markets. It is an umbrella covering internal and external fraud, money laundering and terrorism financing.
cards.originalText: Any criminal conduct relating to money or to financial services or markets

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Selection is one of the four components of a framework to control internal fraud.
cards.explanation: The four components of internal fraud management are selection, prevention, detection and deterrents.
cards.originalText: Selection

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Placement is one of the four components of a framework to control internal fraud.
cards.explanation: Placement is the first phase of money laundering, not a fraud control. The four components are selection, prevention, detection and deterrents.
cards.originalText: Placement
cards.correction: Selection is one of the four components of a framework to control internal fraud.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Legal pursuits fall under the deterrents step of AML controls.
cards.explanation: Deterrents are punitive actions such as legal pursuits, account closure and referral to the financial intelligence unit, which tip the risk-reward balance against laundering.
cards.originalText: Legal pursuits

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: A transaction monitoring system is a deterrents control within AML controls.
cards.explanation: Transaction monitoring is a detection control. Deterrents are announced sanctions such as legal pursuits and account closure.
cards.originalText: Transaction monitoring system
cards.correction: A transaction monitoring system is a detection control within AML controls.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Staff information and training is a deterrents control within AML controls.
cards.explanation: Staff information and training is a prevention control. Deterrents are sanctions such as legal pursuits and account closure.
cards.originalText: Staff information and training
cards.correction: Staff information and training is a prevention control within AML controls.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Placement is one of the phases of money laundering.
cards.explanation: Money laundering proceeds through placement, layering and integration (also called extraction).
cards.originalText: Placement

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Detection is one of the phases of money laundering.
cards.explanation: Detection is a step of AML controls, not a laundering phase. The phases are placement, layering and integration.
cards.originalText: Detection
cards.correction: Layering is one of the phases of money laundering.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: In its 2022 review of challenger banks, the FCA found that information gathered at account opening may be insufficient to identify higher-risk customers, so customer identification, verification and risk assessment need to be strengthened.
cards.explanation: Quick, fully digital onboarding can leave too little information to identify higher-risk customers, so the FCA called for stronger identification, verification and risk assessment controls.
cards.originalText: Information gathered at account opening may be insufficient to identify higher‑risk customers, so customer identification, verification and risk assessment need to be strengthened.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: The FCA found that rapid digital onboarding gives challenger banks more information on new customers than traditional banks hold, so higher-risk customers are identified more reliably.
cards.explanation: The FCA found the opposite: speed of onboarding creates a risk that information gathered is insufficient to identify higher-risk customers.
cards.originalText: Rapid digital onboarding gives challenger banks more information on new customers than traditional banks hold, so higher‑risk customers are identified more reliably.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Because challenger banks rely on machine-learning KYC tools, they are exempt from enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons.
cards.explanation: AML rules, including enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons, apply regardless of automation. The FCA actually found enhanced due diligence was applied inconsistently.
cards.originalText: Because challenger banks rely on machine‑learning KYC tools, they are exempt from enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Smurfing involves making a series of frequent small deposits so that each stays below the AML reporting threshold.
cards.explanation: Smurfing is a placement-phase technique that splits a large amount into many small transactions to avoid reporting thresholds and detection.
cards.originalText: The account holder made a series of frequent small deposits into the account.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Smurfing is characterised by a single very large deposit well above the anti-money laundering reporting threshold.
cards.explanation: Smurfing is the opposite: a large amount is broken into many small deposits to stay under the reporting threshold. A single very large deposit would trigger reporting.
cards.originalText: The account holder made a very large deposit into the account, well above the anti‑money laundering (AML) reporting threshold.
cards.correction: Smurfing is characterised by a series of frequent small deposits well below the anti-money laundering reporting threshold.

changes.from: a single very large deposit well above
changes.to: a series of frequent small deposits well below

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Conversion is one of the three phases of money laundering.
cards.explanation: The three phases of money laundering are placement, layering and integration (also called extraction). Conversion is not a recognised phase.
cards.originalText: Conversion.
cards.correction: Layering is one of the three phases of money laundering.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Integration is one of the phases of money laundering.
cards.explanation: Integration is the third phase, in which the cleaned funds re-enter the economy as apparently legitimate wealth.
cards.originalText: Integration.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.statement: Layering is one of the phases of money laundering.
cards.explanation: Layering is the second phase, in which the origin of the funds is obscured through multiple, complex transactions.
cards.originalText: Layering.

cards.subject: Operational Risk
cards.topic: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
cards.loText: Describe elements of a control framework to manage financial fraud risk and money laundering risk.
cards.reading: ORR-11: Financial Crime and Fraud
